input.question: if DNA is being damaged as you get older how can an old man, and there is cases of people with 80 years old or more, have a son and this son is like all other babies, new and fresh?
input.ground_truth: It's all thanks to a wonderful enzyme called telomerase. DNA gets shorter every time it divides, so it has long non coding regions on the ends called telomeres. These shorten too, but because they aren't essential for making anything they don't damage you until they actually run out. When producing sperm and eggs telomerase is active and gives each bit of DNA brand new telomeres even as the older people have telomeres that run out. Plants have telomerase activity at their growth nodes throughout their entire life, which is why when you take cuttings those are new and fresh too.

Okay, let’s imagine DNA is like a special instruction book inside every tiny cell in your body. This book tells your body how to grow and work.

When you get really old, sometimes the pages of your instruction book can get a little torn or messy. But when you want to have a baby, your body uses a special way to make new instruction books for the baby.

When a man and a woman want to have a baby, they each give half of their instruction books (called genes) to make a brand new one for the baby. The body is very careful when it does this, and it tries to fix any little mistakes or torn pages as much as it can.

That’s why the baby is fresh and new, even if the parents are old. The baby gets a new instruction book, almost like a brand new book, not the old, torn one. That’s why babies are always new and fresh, no matter how old their parents are!
